identification.summary: AVIVORE is a threat group named by Context Information Security in October 2019 after it investigated attacks on multinational enterprises that compromised smaller engineering and consultancy suppliers in their supply chains [S2][S3]. Context described the activity as 'horizontal' island hopping through connectivity between supply-chain partners [S3].
identification.firstObserved: Publicly named in 2019-10 [S2][S3]. Earlier start dates (summer 2018) could not be verified and were removed.
identification.notes: Context's name only. No Microsoft name, MITRE group ID or other vendor aliases were found in the sources reviewed. Initial press reporting on Airbus suppliers had floated APT10 or the Jiangsu State Security Department (JSSD); Context disputed this and treated AVIVORE as a separate group that shares some similarities with APT10/JSSD [S3]. Keep AVIVORE separate from APT10 unless a source merges them.

attribution.confidence: Context assessed with moderate confidence that the campaign's objective is intellectual property theft [S3]. Context stopped short of blaming China, but said the group operates in the same time zone and shares some similarities with APT10/JSSD [S3]. ETDA's threat card lists the actor as China-linked [S6]; this is a secondary catalogue entry, not a vendor or government attribution.
attribution.basis: Context's own investigation of multiple intrusions, with similarities to APT10/JSSD and a matching time zone of activity [S3]. No government attribution found.
attribution.note: Country 'CN' in the record is inherited from the import and is supported only by secondary reporting [S6].

objectives: Context assessed with moderate confidence that the aim is intellectual property theft [S3].

targeting.notes: Context described incidents against UK and European aerospace and defence in which both large primes and smaller engineering or consultancy secondary firms were victims [S3]. Context also saw AVIVORE target assets in automotive, consultancy, energy/nuclear and space and satellite technology [S3]. Press reporting linked the Airbus supplier attacks to Rolls-Royce and Expleo; this link rests on press reporting, not on Context naming victims.

capabilities.summary: Context said the group abuses legitimate remote connectivity and collaboration tools (including commercial VPNs) shared between large firms and their suppliers to bypass well-defended perimeters [S3]. ETDA lists PlugX, Mimikatz and living-off-the-land techniques [S6]; this rests on a secondary catalogue, not a primary Context statement I could open.

campaigns.name: Context names AVIVORE
campaigns.summary: Context publicly identified AVIVORE as the group behind a multi-vertical campaign, disputed the APT10 attribution, assessed IP theft as the objective with moderate confidence, and noted targeting beyond aerospace [S2][S3].

diamond.adversary: AVIVORE, a group named by Context with no stated sponsor; similarities to APT10/JSSD and same time zone noted [S3].
diamond.capability: Abuse of legitimate remote connectivity and collaboration tools; PlugX reported by secondary sources [S3][S6].
diamond.infrastructure: Abuse of commercial VPNs and collaboration platforms as trust paths between organizations [S3]. Adversary-owned infrastructure not described in sources reviewed.
diamond.victim: Aerospace and defence primes and smaller engineering/consultancy suppliers, plus automotive, energy/nuclear and space/satellite assets in the UK and Europe [S3].
diamond.socioPolitical: Intellectual property theft assessed with moderate confidence by Context; sponsor not named [S3].
diamond.technology: Inter-company VPNs, remote access and collaboration tools [S3].

gaps: No state sponsor is stated by any source reviewed; China link is inferred from similarity to APT10/JSSD and time zone [S3].
Context's primary post/press release and Computer Weekly article could not be confirmed in search results; sources removed.
Exact publication dates of several sources are unverified beyond month.
Link between AVIVORE and the named Airbus suppliers comes from press reporting.
No malware, IOC or infrastructure details from a primary source; PlugX association unverified.
Start of activity unverified (summer 2018 claim removed; one search summary suggested possibly as early as 2015).
No activity reporting after 2019-10 found; current status unknown.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. The relevant terrain is the trusted inter-company connectivity (VPNs, collaboration tools) between defence primes and small suppliers [S3]. Threat: an actor abusing legitimate remote access, with moderate-confidence IP-theft intent [S3]. Candidate indicators: anomalous supplier VPN logins and PlugX-style activity (secondary source) [S3][S6].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Defence industrial base suppliers, including small engineering firms, are likely entry points, so supplier incident reporting should feed the common operating picture [S3]. Segment and monitor partner VPN links; share indicators with suppliers and allied counterparts since victims span nations [S3].
